User permission. valid values: all_squash, no_all_squash, root_squash, no_root_squash. default value: root_squash.
All_squash: all accessing users (including the root user) will be mapped to anonymous users or groups.
no_all_squash: all accessing users (including the root user) retain original UID/GID information.
root_squash: maps visiting root user to anonymous user or user group. non-root user keeps original UID/GID information.
no_root_squash: has the same effect as no_all_squash. all accessing users (including the root user) retain their original UID/GID information.

members.document:
create: creates a directory, equivalent to mkdir.
check: checks whether a directory exists, equivalent to stat.
move: renames a file or directory, equivalent to mv.
members.name: OpetationType

members.document:
The system recursively creates all parent directories in the path by default. The path must start with /cfs/, which represents the logical path inside the file storage instance, not the local mount point path.
Example:

  • If the operation is create/check

    • If the CFS root directory / is mounted, and you need to create/check whether test1/test2 exists under the mount path, the input value is /cfs/test1/test2
    • If the CFS subdirectory /subdir is mounted, and you need to create/check whether test1/test2 exists under the mount path, the input value is /cfs/subdir/test1/test2

  • If the operation is move

    • If the CFS root directory / is mounted, and you need to move files under test1/test2 to DestPath, the input value is /cfs/test1/test2
    • If the CFS subdirectory /subdir is mounted, and you need to move files under test1/test2 to DestPath, the input value is /cfs/subdir/test1/test2
members.name: DirectoryPath

members.document: Permission for creating the directory. If not specified, the default value is 0755. If OperationType is check, this value is meaningless.
members.name: Mode

members.document:
Target directory path for the mv operation. It must start with /cfs/, which represents the logical path inside the file storage instance, not the local mount point path.
Example:

  • If the CFS root directory / is mounted, and you need to move files under DirectoryPath to test3/test4 under the mount path, the input value is /cfs/test3/test4
  • If the CFS subdirectory /subdir is mounted, and you need to move files under DirectoryPath to test3/test4 under the mount path, the input value is /cfs/subdir/test3/test4
members.name: DestPath

members.document: 1: success. 0: failure. For the operation of creating a directory, 1 indicates that the directory is created successfully, and 0 indicates a creation failure. For the operation of checking whether a directory exists, 1 indicates that the directory exists, and 0 indicates that the directory does not exist. In addition, if the directory already exists during the directory creation operation, the creation is also considered successful.
